title: Staging the Next Invocation
summary: Work through Staging the Next Invocation.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Staging the Next Invocation** in *Context Engineering* (Vol III).

blocks.source: Vol III, Context Engineering, § Staging the Next Invocation
blocks.md: In our connection-pool repair task, the selected manifest holds several distinct kinds of material: public API constraints, source excerpts from `src/pool.py` at revision `r17`, test results from `test_waiter_notified_on_return`, and the missed-notification working hypothesis alongside an abandoned timeout explanation. Concatenating these items into a flat, unlabeled string would blur the distinctions that guide the model's next decision. Once a selection policy chooses the working set for an upcoming call, staging turns those entries into a structured request payload.

blocks.title: Map of the section
blocks.md:
The section is organised as:

- Ordering by change rate
- Preserving source and scope
- Preserving an exact prefix

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Context compaction matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Every compaction is a lossy transform that can silently drop evidence a later decision needs, so the runtime pins a protected-field set and keeps handles to raw records.

questions.q: The section **Staging the Next Invocation** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Usable context is an empirical property of a model, configuration, representation, and workload found by decision-level evaluation, because attention dilutes a target key as staged keys accumulate and position matters.

Staging the request as root, trunk, and leaf by change rate keeps the longest exact token prefix reusable, so volatile fields belong in the leaf, although correctness always overrides cache economics.
An observation is evidence only for the artifact versions and execution conditions under which it was gathered, and provenance labels on untrusted spans guide interpretation but enforce nothing.
Every compaction is a lossy transform that can silently drop evidence a later decision needs, so the runtime pins a protected-field set and keeps handles to raw records.
